summary: Tenant-aware controlled degradation guidance for optimizer profiles
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NexaHealth reported increased 95th/99th percentile token latency and occasional hallucination-like quality regressions after enabling a tenant-scoped optimizer bundle (aggressive batching + KV-prefetch + 4-bit quant profile) on Dedicated capacity. Customer wants a safe, tenant-aware plan to reduce optimizer aggressiveness without causing throughput collapse or wide-blast configuration changes across other tenants.

Impact:
- Multiple user-facing endpoints saw 95p token latency go from ~150ms to ~420ms for tenant NexaHealth over the past 8 hours.
- Some inference outputs for multi-turn chat degraded (truncated tokens / missing context) after switching to quant profile v2.
- Customer-facing SLAs at risk; affect limited to their dedicated pool but rollback needs to be tenant-scoped.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-4 (cuda-rt v2.8)
- Region: us-east-1
- Tenant config snapshot: optimizer: {batch_target: 256, kv_prefetch: enabled, quant_profile: q4v2-aggr}
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Apply tenant optimizer bundle (batch_target=256, kv_prefetch=on, quant=q4v2-aggr) via /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant}/optimizer-config
2) Route steady chat workload with typical seq_len=512 and p95 request burst
3) Observe increase in p95/p99 token latency and occasional truncated generation in console traces
4) Revert only quant_profile to q8-safe and notice partial recovery but throughput drops
logs_and_evidence:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/dedicated-pool?orgId=1&var-pool=dp-us-east-4 (p95 spike at 2026-03-10T06:12Z)
- Sample runtime logs (truncated):
  [2026-03-10T06:12:03Z] tenant=nexahealth request_id=req-9b3a token_latency=412ms batch_wait=187ms kv_prefetch_miss=0.12
  [2026-03-10T06:12:03Z] allocator: high_cuda_mem_pressure=true free_mem_mb=420
- Console traces: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/nexahealth/traces/req-9b3a
comments: 2026-03-10 07:02 - Support (Aisha): Thanks for the report, we've escalated to SRE to validate pool health and get a safe downgrade plan that is tenant-level only.

2026-03-10 08:45 - SRE (Miguel): Initial hypothesis: interaction between large batch_target and kv-prefetch is causing head-of-line blocking under certain seq_len distributions. We'll run a staged degradation plan and provide a rollback script.
Reference dashboards attached.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (Ioana, NexaHealth): Appreciate the quick response. We can't afford a full pool rollback because other tenants rely on current throughput. Please ensure tenant-scoped changes only.
2026-03-11 03:12 - Support (Aisha): Drafted tenant-scoped plan, testing on staging with a copy of their traffic profile. Plan attached below.
2026-03-12 09:10 - SRE (Miguel): Began controlled degradation on a single shard for tenant; monitoring shows p95 reduced to ~180ms so far. Continuing roll-forward cautiously.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between batch_target spikes and allocator memory pressure; larger batches increase KV cache miss amplification for long sequences.
Hypothesis: q4v2-aggr quant profile accelerates compute but reduces numerical headroom for KV cache alignment leading to increased micro-retries and token emission stalls under bursty loads.
Tested lowering batch_target from 256->192->144 in staging with representative load; p95 improved incrementally without throughput collapse.
Checked autoscaler logs: no unexpected scale-downs during incident window. Scheduler queues show per-tenant queuing rose ~3x when optimizer bundle enabled.
proposed_action_plan:
1) Immediate tenant-level mitigation (can be executed without pool restart):
   - Reduce tenant batch_target by 40% in 3 steps (256 -> 192 -> 144 -> 96) with 10-minute observation windows.
   - Disable kv_prefetch for tenant if latency not improving after first step.
   - Revert quant_profile to q8-stable for tenant as fallback.
2) Use rolling shard approach: apply change to 1 shard of tenant (shard-2) then expand after stable metrics.
3) Monitor 95/99p token latency, token_throughput, and kv_prefetch_hit_rate dashboards; hold if p95 increases or errors increase.
4) If degradation fails to recover, execute tenant snapshot restore to known-good config saved at 2026-03-09T22:14Z.
Canary metrics to watch: tenant_p95_token_latency, tenant_error_5xx_rate, tenant_generation_abort_rate, allocator_free_mem_mb
resolution_notes:
In-progress: Applied first decrement to batch_target on shard-2 at 2026-03-12T09:00Z. p95 decreased from 420ms->210ms after first step.
Next steps: continue with 2nd decrement if stable for 15 minutes, otherwise disable kv_prefetch next.
No full pool changes required; actions are tenant-scoped as requested by customer.
Rollback path: tenant-config-snapshot-20260309 (automated restore available via console)
follow_up_actions: 1) Add preflight simulation in Console when applying aggressive optimizer bundles that predicts per-tenant queuing and memory headroom.
2) Add an automated guardian that prevents enabling q4v2-aggr if average seq_len > 384 for tenant.
3) Create a KB article: 'Tenant-scoped optimizer de-escalation playbook' and link from support responses.
4) Post-incident retro scheduled with SRE and Product to consider safer default quant profiles for Dedicated customers.
notes_for_engineering: Look into KV prefetch alignment heuristics for q4 quant profiles; possible kernel-level fix to avoid amplification of cache misses for long-seq workloads.
Consider adding per-tenant token_budget admission control so single tenant can't push oversized batch targets beyond safe memory headroom.
